reviews.title: Watch out for auto renewals
reviews.text: I canceled my subscription over a year ago, and thought that that was sufficient. I was wrong, I was somehow reactivated and was charged a significant amount more not through my card but through my PayPal. I called immediately asking to please refund my money but they said they would not. It was an awful experience they said they would give me 69% back. Yet I was charged $107 then week later $117. reviews.title: CONSUMER BEWARE!!
reviews.text: CONSUMER BEWARE!!! I paid for a two-year subscription during a promo for ipVanish in April of 2025. In March of this year (2026), while adding one of the TVs in my house to my account, I noticed what the renewal price for one year was going to be (a LOT!) so I decided I was not going to continue service with them after my two-year subscription ended. At that time, I still had a bit over one year left, so while I wasn't in a hurry, I began looking for how to remove my payment information from their site so I didn't forget and end up being charged an exorbitant amount later. The platform is *not* user friendly, and no matter where I looked, I could not find where to change or remove my payment information. I contacted support, who did respond timely and provided instructions for canceling my membership - which they said would not happen until my current paid term was up (April, 2027). Great! Life was life'ing and it wasn't until about 3 months later that I finally got back around to logging back in and following their instructions, which I did to the tee. It brought me to the cancellation screen, however, their system would not let me save the changes, continuing to pop up an error message telling me that I could not cancel, and to "contact support." Ok, frustrating. I responded to the same email chain I had with "CJ," who I had gone back and forth with multiple times by this point. reviews.title: Unethical Company
reviews.text:
I tested the "free trial" to see if this was a company I could trust. It wasn't.
First, they force you into a $90 yearly plan just to access the trial—already suspicious. I signed up, but decided within the week that I’d prefer a month-to-month commitment. I did the routine thing: I hit cancel subscription in my Apple settings. The system confirmed my access would expire at the end of the week.
Instead, IPVanish killed my account the second they realized I wasn't going to be their $90 cash cow. The economy is trashed; yearly subs are a gamble nobody should be taking right now. These greedy, untrustworthy pigs need to read their developer terms of service, which strictly forbids killing access before a trial period ends. They broke the contract, not I.
I will never trust this company or any service they ever offer. If you can’t trust your VPN provider to be on the up and up, who can you trust? note: these guys front loaded a bunch of fake 5 star reviews. To get the real user experience, sort reviews by “most recent”.

reviews.title: Shady
reviews.text: I originally purchased an IPVanish subscription before deploying in 2023. When I returned, I cancelled the subscription through the app and assumed it was taken care of. To my surprise, I later discovered I had been charged for nearly three years after that. I went back and cancelled again through the app, only to be charged for another additional month because apparently the cancellation also required confirmation through an email link. That process wasn’t clear at all during cancellation. Requiring an extra confirmation step through email after cancelling in the app feels misleading and honestly shady. Just be careful and make sure you fully verify the cancellation process or you may continue getting billed.

reviews.title: Shady Cancellation Practice
reviews.text:
The VPN itself was okay, but the cancellation process is extremely frustrating and feels intentionally obstructive.

The “cancel subscription” button on their website did nothing, and the contact support button also failed to work. I was only able to reach support by modifying my subscription first and using a link from the confirmation email.

Once connected, support pushed retention offers and delayed cancellation. Ultimately, I had to revoke PayPal’s automatic payment authorization entirely just to ensure I wouldn’t be charged again.

Needing to cancel billing externally because a company’s own cancellation system doesn’t function is not acceptable. This experience alone is why I would not recommend the service.
